memory_verse.label: Bible Reference

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before any annual festival is listed, God begins with the weekly one.
Rest comes first. Once every seven days, everything stopped.

Notice the phrase "wherever you live." You did not need to travel to
the tabernacle for this. Sabbath came to the village, the field, the
ordinary house. It was portable holiness.

For a people freshly out of Egypt, this was staggering. Slaves do not
get days off. God was teaching them that their identity was no longer
"workforce." They were His people, and their worth did not rest on
their output.

Dear reader, that lesson has not aged. We live in a world that measures
people by productivity. Rest feels like falling behind. Yet God built
rest into creation itself before sin ever entered the world.

Christians have differed for centuries on exactly how the Sabbath
applies today, and sincere believers land in different places. But the
principle underneath is not in dispute: we were not made to run
without stopping. Jesus said the Sabbath was made for man, not man for
the Sabbath (Mark 2:27), and He offers a deeper rest still - come to
me, all you who are weary, and I will give you rest (Matt 11:28).

Stop this week. Your worth is not in your work.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last genuinely stop and rest without guilt?
2. Do I secretly believe my value comes from what I produce?
3. What would a restful, God-centred day look like in my life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I confess how easily I tie my worth to how much I do. Teach me
to rest in You, and thank You for the deeper rest Jesus gives. Amen.
